newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC Hldgs sees easing in mortgage market.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Hldgs sees easing in mortgage market.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd has noted an easing in the residential property market and sees demand for mortgages declining in the second half of the year, senior executives said on Tuesday.

"We are pleased to see the levelling off that has taken place in the property market. This is good and healthy for Hong Kong," John Strickland, chairman of Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd, said at a news conference.
The meeting following an HSBC Holdings Plc shareholders' meeting in Hong Kong, held prior to the bank's annual general meeting in London.

"We are comfortable with our exposure to the residential mortgage market," Strickland said. "Many of our loans were made when property values were a bit lower than they are at the moment, so the loan to value ratio of our portfolio is very acceptable."

Strickland said the banks' total exposure to the property market, including loans to building and construction companies and commercial property loans, would be approximately 40 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio.
"However, we agree with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority that some slowing in property price rises would be desirable," Strickland added.
Property prices and activity in the residential property market cooled in April following a rise in lending rates by Hong Kong banks at the end of March.
But sales activity has picked up sharply in May, sparking the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to reiterate its call for banks to maintain prudent lending criteria.
On Monday, the authority said additional restraints in mortgage lending policies may be required as growth in lending has resulted in an increase in banks' property exposure.
"It is perfectly reasonable for the HKMA to recommend prudential limits for mortgage lending," HSBC Holdings group chief executive John Bond said.

Gross new loans made in Hong Kong during April increased by 35.2 percent to a record high of HK$22.7 billion, and new loans approved during April rose by 36.4 percent to HK$28.8 billion, reflecting the large scale of market activity in March, the authority said.
The bank had sustained its market share in home loans in Hong Kong, Bond said, but he did not give any other details.
